passages.scripture: Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus, called to be an apostle, and set apart for the gospel of God— the gospel He promised beforehand through His prophets in the Holy Scriptures, regarding His Son, who was a descendant of David according to the flesh, and who through the Spirit of holiness was declared with power to be the Son of God by His resurrection from the dead: Jesus Christ our Lord.

lines.text: Paul serves Christ Jesus.
God called Paul to be an apostle.
God set Paul apart for the gospel of God.
God promised this gospel long ago.
God spoke this promise through His prophets.
These promises are written in the Holy Scriptures.
The gospel is about God’s Son.
God’s Son was born as a descendant of David.
God’s Son was born as a human being.
God’s Son is Jesus Christ.
God raised Jesus Christ from the dead.
God declared Jesus Christ to be His Son by raising Him from the dead.
God raised Jesus to life through His power and the Spirit of holiness.
The Spirit of holiness is Holy Spirit.
Jesus Christ is our Lord.

passages.scripture: Through Him and on behalf of His name, we received grace and apostleship to call all those among the Gentiles to the obedience that comes from faith.

lines.text: God called Paul to be an apostle.
God gave grace and apostleship through Jesus Christ.
Paul received this grace and apostleship for a purpose.
The purpose is to call people from all nations.
All these nations are called to obey God.
This obedience comes from faith.
Paul does this work for the name of Jesus Christ.

passages.scripture: And you also are among those who are called to belong to Jesus Christ.

lines.text: There are people whom Jesus Christ has called to belong to Him.
You are among those whom Jesus Christ has called.
Jesus Christ calls you to belong to Him.

passages.scripture: To all in Rome who are loved by God and called to be saints: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

lines.text: Paul writes to the people in Rome.
These people live in the city of Rome.
God loves these people.
God calls these people to be saints.
Paul greets these people.
Paul says, “Grace to you.”
Paul says, “Peace to you.”
Grace and peace come from God our Father.
Grace and peace come from the Lord Jesus Christ.

passages.scripture: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is being proclaimed all over the world.

lines.text: Paul writes to the Christians in Rome.
Paul thanks his God for them.
Paul gives thanks through Jesus Christ.
Paul gives thanks for all the believers in Rome.
People everywhere talk about the faith of the Roman Christians.
The faith of the Roman Christians is known throughout the whole world.

passages.scripture: God, whom I serve with my spirit in preaching the gospel of His Son, is my witness how constantly I remember you in my prayers at all times, asking that now at last by God’s will I may succeed in coming to you.

lines.text: God is the witness of Paul.
Paul serves God with his spirit.
Paul serves God by preaching the gospel of His Son.
Paul always mentions these Roman Christians in his prayers.
God knows how Paul remembers these Roman Christians constantly in his prayers.
Paul asks God that Paul may finally succeed in coming to these Roman Christians.
Paul prays this will happen by God’s will.

passages.scripture: For I long to see you so that I may impart to you some spiritual gift to strengthen you, that is, that you and I may be mutually encouraged by each other’s faith.

lines.text: Paul desires to visit the believers in Rome.
Paul wants to see them.
Paul wants to give them a spiritual gift.
Paul wants this gift to make them strong.
Paul also wants both himself and the believers to be encouraged.
Paul says their faith and his faith will encourage each other.

passages.scripture: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, how often I planned to come to you (but have been prevented from visiting until now), in order that I might have a harvest among you, just as I have had among the other Gentiles.

lines.text: Paul is speaking to his brothers in Christ
Paul wants his brothers to know something important.
Paul had often planned to come to his brothers in Rome.
When Paul wrote the letter of Romans, Paul had not yet been able to visit these brothers in Rome.
Paul wanted to come to Rome so Paul could have a harvest among the brothers in Rome.
Paul has had a harvest among other Gentiles.
Paul wanted to also have a harvest among these brothers in Rome.

passages.scripture: I am obligated both to Greeks and non-Greeks, both to the wise and the foolish.

lines.text: Paul is obligated to deliver the gospel to all Gentiles.
Paul is obligated to deliver the gospel to Greeks.
Paul is also obligated to deliver the gospel to non-Greeks.
Paul is obligated to deliver the gospel to the wise.
Paul is also obligated to deliver the gospel to the foolish.

passages.scripture: That is why I am so eager to preach the gospel also to you who are in Rome.

lines.text: There are people who are in the city of Rome.
Paul is obligated to deliver the gospel to all Gentiles.
Those in Rome are among the Gentiles.
Therefore Paul is obligated to deliver the gospel to those in Rome.
And Paul is eager to preach the gospel to those who are in Rome.

passages.scripture: I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, first to the Jew, then to the Greek.

lines.text: Paul is not ashamed of the gospel.
We should not be ashamed of the the gospel, either.
The gospel is the message about Jesus Christ.
The gospel is the power of God.
God uses the gospel to bring salvation.
Salvation is for everyone who believes.
God offers salvation first to the Jew.
God also offers salvation to the Greek.

passages.scripture: For the gospel reveals the righteousness of God that comes by faith from start to finish, just as it is written: “The righteous will live by faith.”

lines.text: The gospel reveals the righteousness of God.
This righteousness comes by faith.
Faith is necessary from beginning to end.
Scripture says, “The righteous will live by faith.”

passages.scripture: The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wickedness of men who suppress the truth by their wickedness.

lines.text: God reveals His wrath from heaven.
God’s wrath comes against all godlessness.
God’s wrath comes against all wickedness of people.
These people suppress the truth by their wickedness.

passages.scripture: For what may be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them.

lines.text: God exists.
God has made Himself known to people.
People can know things about God.
God has shown these things clearly to people.
What can be known about God is obvious to people.
God Himself has made it obvious.

passages.scripture: For since the creation of the world God’s invisible qualities, His eternal power and divine nature, have been clearly seen, being understood from His workmanship, so that men are without excuse.

lines.text: God has invisible qualities.
God has eternal power.
God has divine nature.
God created the world.
People can see God’s qualities since the world was made.
People understand God’s qualities by looking at what God made.
People have no excuse for not knowing about God.

passages.scripture: For although they knew God, they neither glorified Him as God nor gave thanks to Him, but they became futile in their thinking and darkened in their foolish hearts.

lines.text: The people knew God.
But they did not glorify God as God.
They did not give thanks to God.
Their thinking became useless.
Their foolish hearts became dark.

passages.scripture: Although they claimed to be wise, they became fools, and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images of mortal man and birds and animals and reptiles.

lines.text: People claimed to be wise.
They said they had wisdom.
But they became fools.
They did not keep true wisdom.
God is immortal.
God cannot die or become weak.
Nothing is more glorious than God.
The glory of God is above all other glory.
And yet they exchanged the glory of God.
They gave up God’s glory for images.
They chose images that look like mortal people.
They chose images of birds.
They chose images of animals with four legs.
They chose images of reptiles.
They worshiped created things instead of the immortal God.

passages.scripture: Therefore God gave them over in the desires of their hearts to impurity for the dishonoring of their bodies with one another.

lines.text: God allowed these people follow the desires of their hearts.
Their desires led them to impurity.
They dishonored their bodies with one another.

passages.scripture: They exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is forever worthy of praise! Amen.

lines.text: Some people rejected the truth of God.
They chose a lie instead.
They worshiped created things.
They served what was created.
They did not worship the Creator.
God is the Creator.
God is forever worthy of praise.
Amen.

passages.scripture: For this reason God gave them over to dishonorable passions. Even their women exchanged natural relations for unnatural ones.

lines.text: God gave some people over to dishonorable passions.
Their women exchanged natural relations for unnatural ones.

passages.scripture: Likewise, the men abandoned natural relations with women and burned with lust for one another. Men committed indecent acts with other men, and received in themselves the due penalty for their error.

lines.text: Some men abandoned natural relations with women.
These men burned with lust for one another.
They acted indecently with other men.
They received in themselves the penalty their error deserved.

passages.scripture: Furthermore, since they did not see fit to acknowledge God, He gave them up to a depraved mind, to do what ought not to be done.

lines.text: These people refused to acknowledge God.
God responded to their choice.
God gave them over to a depraved mind.
They began to do things that should not be done.

passages.scripture: They have become filled with every kind of wickedness, evil, greed, and depravity. They are full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, and malice. They are gossips, slanderers, God-haters, insolent, arrogant, and boastful. They invent new forms of evil; they disobey their parents.

lines.text: These people have become completely wicked.
They are full of every kind of evil.
They are greedy.
They are depraved.
They are full of envy.
They are full of murder.
They are full of strife.
They are full of deceit.
They are full of malice.
They gossip.
They slander others.
They hate God.
They are insolent.
They are arrogant.
They are boastful.
They invent new ways to do evil.
They disobey their parents.

passages.scripture: They are senseless, faithless, heartless, merciless.

lines.text: These people are senseless.
They do not understand what is right.
They are faithless.
They do not keep their promises.
They are heartless.
They do not show love or care for others.
They are merciless.
They do not show compassion or kindness.

passages.scripture: Although they know God’s righteous decree that those who do such things are worthy of death, they not only continue to do these things, but also approve of those who practice them.

lines.text: These people know God’s righteous decree.
They understand what God requires.
They know that people who do such things deserve death.
But they keep doing these things.
They also approve of others who do them.
